subsystems.name: Pressure hull and thermal insulation
subsystems.role: protects electronics from the cryogenic liquid and pressure at depth.

subsystems.name: Power system
subsystems.role: provides electricity and heat in the extreme cold.
parts: radioisotope thermal generator or Stirling generator

subsystems.name: Propulsion and buoyancy
subsystems.role: moves the vehicle through liquid methane and controls depth.

subsystems.name: Communication system
subsystems.role: sends data to a surface lander by acoustic link.

subsystems.name: Science payload
subsystems.role: characterises dissolved organics, seafloor composition, and wave dynamics.

subsystems.name: Command and data handling
subsystems.role: enables autonomous navigation and data processing.

buildSteps.title: Study Kraken Mare
buildSteps.detail: Use Cassini radar data and Earth-based observations to map depth, composition, and conditions in the sea.

buildSteps.title: Design the vehicle
buildSteps.detail: Set hull thickness, power, and thermal requirements for 94 kelvin and up to roughly 15 bar at depth.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate and test components
buildSteps.detail: Test electronics and materials in liquid methane simulants at cryogenic temperatures.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and integrate
buildSteps.detail: Build the submersible and its surface lander, then test the system in a thermal vacuum chamber.

buildSteps.title: Launch and cruise
buildSteps.detail: Send the spacecraft to Saturn on a multi-year trajectory, possibly using gravity assists.

buildSteps.title: Entry, descent, and landing
buildSteps.detail: An aeroshell decelerates the craft, a parachute deploys, and the lander splashes down and floats.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and dive
buildSteps.detail: The submarine separates, activates, and begins exploring Kraken Mare, sending acoustic data to the lander for relay to Earth.

buildSteps.title: Operate and survive
buildSteps.detail: Conduct a mission of perhaps weeks to months, managing power and thermal limits in the alien sea.

prerequisites.why: radioisotope generators have powered deep-space missions, but must be adapted for operation in liquid methane.
not yet demonstrated in Titan conditions, and radio waves do not propagate through liquid methane.
terrestrial autonomous underwater vehicles exist, but Titan's communication delay requires full autonomy.
some metals and polymers are known to resist, but long-term immersion data is lacking.
launch vehicles and the Deep Space Network are operational and can support a Saturn mission.

pathway.milestone: concept studies refine mission architecture and instrument needs
pathway.unlocks: a clear set of technology gaps to address.

pathway.milestone: cryogenic testing of subsystems in liquid methane simulants
pathway.unlocks: validated components for a flight proposal.

pathway.milestone: mission proposal to a space agency and selection
pathway.unlocks: funded development and a target launch date.

pathway.milestone: launch and cruise to Titan over several years

pathway.unlocks: first direct measurements of an extraterrestrial sea.
